Observed RMSE is not a uniform error guarantee. Full catalog values require paid continuation experiments on bounded cases; unrestricted alternatives are unknown. The inequality diagnoses one decision and does not establish global regret or policy improvement. Solver gap under its additive surrogate is a separate computational quantity.

G.6.2 Seeded Refinement

For m≥1m\geq 1 extensions forming feasible job sets A0⊂⋯⊂AmA_{0}\subset\cdots\subset A_{m}, set W⁡(A)=Q^ϕ¯​(S~,VERIFY​(A))W(A)=\widehat{Q}_{\bar{\phi}}(\widetilde{S},\textsc{VERIFY}(A)) at one fixed proposal state. Then

∑t=1m[W⁡(At)−W⁡(At−1)]=W⁡(Am)−W⁡(A0).\sum_{t=1}^{m}[W(A_{t})-W(A_{t-1})]=W(A_{m})-W(A_{0}).

The equality holds without additivity or submodularity. Unlike summing W⁡(Dj)W(D_{j}), it does not repeatedly add the same base continuation. However, positive single-job increments can still miss bundles: with two jobs of unit cost, gain g>2​λg>2\lambda, and a fixed continuation that stops immediately after the offered work, W⁡(∅)=0W(\varnothing)=0, W⁡({a})=W⁡({b})=−λW(\{a\})=W(\{b\})=-\lambda, and W⁡({a,b})=g−2​λ>0W(\{a,b\})=g-2\lambda>0. Empty-seed positive-gain greedy stops; an affordable complete-candidate seed presents the pair to the actor. This verifies the purpose of the seed family, not a general approximation ratio. Higher-order cross-candidate interactions and inaccurate WW remain limitations.

G.7 Learning Identities

G.7.1 Policy-Gradient Baseline

Fix the initial state, verification contract Γ\Gamma, menu settings ν\nu, scorer snapshot ϕ¯k\bar{\phi}_{k}, and support rules. Let ϑ=(θ,ψ)\vartheta=(\theta,\psi) contain only the sampled edit/plan parameters, τ\tau a full search trajectory, PϑP_{\vartheta} its induced law, and R⁡(τ)R(\tau) its realized return. With the typed probabilities of Equation (19) and the usual differentiability, integrability, and fixed-support conditions,

∇ϑ𝔼τ∼Pϑ​R​(τ)=𝔼⁡[Rg​∑j=1Jg∇ϑ​log​pϑ​(yg,j∣Hg,j,𝒴g,j)].\nabla_{\vartheta}\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim P_{\vartheta}}R(\tau)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[R_{g}\sum_{j=1}^{J_{g}}\nabla_{\vartheta}\log p_{\vartheta}(y_{g,j}\mid H_{g,j},\mathcal{Y}_{g,j})\right].

A deterministic menu generator may depend on observed history; its parameters are held fixed here and it contributes no sampled likelihood. Random environment outcomes likewise have no actor likelihood. For GG conditionally independent searches, the baseline bg=(G−1)−1​∑u≠gRub_{g}=(G-1)^{-1}\sum_{u\neq g}R_{u} is independent of trajectory gg conditional on the common start and snapshot. The expectation of bgb_{g} times that trajectory’s score function is zero. Consequently, at ϑk\vartheta_{k}, the expected unclipped group estimator using Ag=Rg−bgA_{g}=R_{g}-b_{g} equals the displayed gradient, with bgb_{g} detached. It is not an identity for gradients through scorer fitting, generator changes, or KL regularization. Clipping remains a surrogate, not a monotonicity guarantee (Ahmadian et al., 2024; Schulman et al., 2017).

Each sampled token and plan contributes once; a deterministic solver contributes none. Dividing each search by JgJ_{g}, reusing shared-tree leaves as independent group members, or differentiating through AgA_{g} changes this estimator. Frozen-menu optimization is the local update in Appendix F.5; refreshed menus require fresh collection. This does not establish global policy improvement or an unbiased off-policy gradient after arbitrary optimization steps.

G.7.2 Contrast Identifiability

At a fixed state and continuation policy, each prospectively forced arm has an ordinary expected return. Independence and fixed sample sizes make its sample mean unbiased. Their difference therefore identifies the conditional contrast in Equation (12). Minimizing population squared difference error identifies that contrast, but is invariant to a common offset added to both predictions. The ordinary return loss in Equation (11) is consequently required to anchor mean calibration. Neither identity establishes data efficiency, actor improvement, or causality of an individual edit. These are separately measured claims.
